# Independent audit: exact mixed-state three-triangle depth

Source: `candidate f89d52b54ff6950f`.

**Result: PASS, all five sections.** No repair identified. The source's
exact verifier passes 1,999 checks. The conclusions remain scoped to
centered homothetic triangles and the stated proper-cell moment identities;
they are not an arbitrary-fiber classification.

## 1. Normal chart and exact cells

A nonzero normal has three triangle vertex heights with sum zero. A
vertex permutation assigns their minimum, maximum, and intermediate
values to the first, second, and third displayed vertices, and positive
rescaling makes the max-minus-min difference equal to three. Thus the
remaining gap ratio is theta in [0,1], producing u=(1,theta) and the
correspondingly rescaled integer coefficient. The permutations preserve
triangle area; this is a legitimate symmetry, not a lattice-mixing map.

The three vertex heights for radius r are -(1+theta)r, (2-theta)r,
and (-1+2theta)r. These give exactly the four threshold statuses in (1).
The two cap formulas agree at k=(1-2theta)r because their respective
heights are 3(1-theta)r and 3theta r. Their alpha derivatives and theta
derivatives agree there too: the common section width is 3r and the
common angular derivative is 3r^2/2. At the empty/full transitions the
vanishing squared height makes all first derivatives zero. Hence the
claimed C^1 property throughout 0<theta<1 includes every transition.

## 2. Moment equations and the complete Hessian

Writing s=1-theta, direct differentiation gives

    d_alpha ell=t/s, d_theta ell=(ell-r)/s       in I,
    d_alpha ell=-t/theta, d_theta ell=-(ell-r)/theta in J.

The gradients are sum ell*t and sum(ell^2/2-r*ell). Their differentiation
therefore yields the signed sum of FULL outer products
(t,ell-r)(t,ell-r)^T, with coefficients 1/s and -1/theta respectively.
In particular the mixed alpha-theta block is included, and no nonnegative
angular curvature alone is mistaken for a local-minimum condition.

The stationarity allocation identities follow algebraically from
sum k*ell=0 and S_I+S_J=2(T_I+T_J):
S_I=3T_I-sT and S_J=3T_J-theta*T. Saturated states contribute zero.
If a concave radius exists on conv(P), the section weights have actual
barycenter z_0, so Jensen gives T<=r(z_0)sum ell. The own section has
positive width, ensuring a nonzero total weight. This is the exact scope
of the extra concavity consequence.

## 3. All angular cases for the three-fiber source

Finite-tilt clamping is valid for the two opposite endpoint offsets;
with a normalized continuous normal all endpoint thresholds beyond one
uniform bound are saturated. It preserves every actual trace and leaves
the source trace unchanged. Cap area is continuous, hence the minimum is
attained on a compact normal parameter set. A purely integer cap is
strictly improved by a finite nonvertical replacement, which retains
strict endpoint statuses and removes positive own-fiber area.

For an interior theta and alpha=0, all centroid sections have width
strictly exceeding twice their fiber radii, so the angular derivative
is positive. Reflection of the integer axis reduces the remaining case
to alpha>0. Integer stationarity forces both endpoint widths to be l.
If l=0, only the strictly positive own angular derivative remains. Thus
no endpoint support transition, full state, or empty state is omitted.
The source width L>2c yields l(D-l)=L(L-2c)/2>0, hence D=a+b>l.

Both endpoints in I imply 2s*l=(2-theta)D and therefore l>D. Both in J
imply 2theta*l=(1+theta)D and again l>D. A left J/right I assignment
would require both theta>1/2 and theta<1/2. Thus only left I/right J is
possible. Their width equations give (10). At a left middle transition,
l=3a would force D=2theta*l/(1+theta)<l; at a right middle transition,
l=3b would force D=2s*l/(2-theta)<l. Hence the endpoint cells are strict.

For theta<1/2, the alpha-alpha Hessian entry 1/s-1/theta is negative.
For theta>1/2, the determinant of the endpoint matrix is
-(D-2l)^2/(s theta), and the source J cell adds the strictly negative
quantity -(L-c)^2(1/s-1/theta)/theta to that determinant. Thus the full
Hessian is not positive semidefinite in either open angular range.

At theta=1/2, stationarity gives a=b. The endpoints remain strict I,J
and the one-sided source cell theta>1/2 is J. Its Hessian has zero
alpha-alpha entry and off-diagonal 2(D-2l). If this is nonzero, a ray
with positive angular component and a suitable finite alpha component
has negative quadratic form and stays in the stated cells for a small
step. If it vanishes, a=b=l and the endpoint angular entries cancel,
while the source contributes -8c^2. The first derivatives vanish and
the one-sided cell formula is smooth up to the boundary, so the stated
one-sided Taylor argument is valid. This handles the source vertex kink.

The complete conclusion follows: every middle-centroid minimizing
continuous normal is canonical or opposite-canonical, for arbitrary
three positive radii. No hidden concavity assumption enters this step.

## 4. Canonical scalar extrema and the opposite normals

The canonical one-fiber function f_r is the exact one-vertex area
between its support levels; it is full at k>=r and empty at k<=-2r.
The joint breakpoints are precisely -a,2a,-2b,b. On a both-proper
interval, g(alpha) is strictly convex with stationary point a-b and
value (a+b)^2. Feasibility is exactly a/2<=b<=2a. Outside that ratio
range the possibly infeasible square candidate exceeds the smaller
saturation value, so retaining it in the displayed minimum is harmless.

At either full transition the derivative jumps downward; it cannot
produce a new local minimum. Empty transitions have continuous first
derivative and add no unlisted minimum. One-proper intervals are monotone,
and plateau values are (9/2)a^2 and (9/2)b^2. For a maximum, only the
full transitions and plateaus are needed, giving exactly (14), including
coincident breakpoints.

Opposite-canonical caps are complements of reversed-tilt canonical caps
up to a line of zero area in every positive fiber. Subtraction from the
full mass gives (15), with coefficient (5/2)c^2 as stated.

For a<=b, the larger maximum candidate is correctly identified: its
difference is 3(b^2-a^2) for b<=2a and (5/2)b^2+2ab-5a^2 for b>=2a.
Under c>=(a+b)/2, the two difference lower bounds in (18) follow by
bounding the canonical minimum by each candidate separately. Their
positive ranges cover all a<=b<2a, including equality a=b and the
junction b=13a/11. For b>=2a the difference is c^2/2>0. Thus no
opposite-canonical minimizer survives actual midpoint compatibility.

## 5. Actual compatibility, all source points, and constants

The radius condition c>=(a+b)/2 is necessary for actual midpoint
containment, and the positive piecewise-affine concave radius constructs
a full-dimensional convex body with exactly those three integer fibers.
The triangle symmetry orbit keeps each base fixed and averages every
continuous point to its actual fiber centroid. Convexity of depth
superlevel sets therefore proves the centroid maximizes each fiber's
depth, without any centroid-rounding step.

At either integer endpoint a finite tilt isolates an ordinary centroid
cap, giving exact endpoint depth 2a^2 or 2b^2. The all-angular calculation
gives the middle value in (19), so their maximum is exactly (20). Every
oblique ambient normal was included before minimizing, and purely
integer boundary mass was treated separately. The normalized denominator
is the actual finite sum (9/2)(a^2+c^2+b^2).

The final 2/9 consistency check is correct after scaling c=1: either the
largest endpoint square is at least the sum of the other two, or both
canonical minimum candidates exceed a^2+b^2-1 and the middle value is
strictly sufficient. The source accurately labels this as a calibration
inside an already covered centered-fiber class, not a new general OC
regime.
